newsitem.title: QATAR: Bahraini air force pilot seeks asylum in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: Bahraini air force pilot seeks asylum in Qatar.

text.p: A Bahraini air force pilot sought political asylum in neighbouring Qatar on Monday after landing his helicopter in the capital Doha, the official Qatar News Agency (QNA) said.

The apparent defection came as year-old tensions between the tiny Gulf Arab states seemed to be easing after Bahrain's Emir Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa pardoned two alleged Qatari spies over the weekend and set them free.

QNA quoted a Qatar foreign ministry source as saying First Lieutenant Nasser Majed Nasser al-Khalifa arrived at Doha International Airport at 4 p.m. (1300 GMT). It added officials were considering his appeal for asylum.
It was not immediately clear if the pilot belonged to Bahrain's al-Khalifa ruling family.
Bahrain's official Gulf News Agency (GNA) said the foreign ministry in Manama had asked Doha to return both the pilot and his helicopter.

GNA said earlier Bahrain's military authorities had been searching for the royal air force transport helicopter, which had left Manama at 2.50 p.m. (1150 GMT). It said the chopper had been on a training flight.

Qatar and Bahrain are locked in a dispute over a cluster of islands, sandbanks and reefs in the Gulf. Manama has controlled the potentially oil and gas-rich territories since the 1930s, but they are also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has taken the case to the International Court of Justice in The Hague, angering Bahrain which prefers an Arab solution.

Ties were further strained this month after Bahrain sentenced two alleged Qatari spies to three years in jail. Bahrain's emir pardoned the two on Saturday. Doha, which had denied they were spies, welcomed the move.
